title: Bonhoeffer and Discipleship in a Broken World
welcome_lead: Walk alongside Dietrich Bonhoeffer from the lecture hall to the conspiracy against Hitler to the cell at Tegel prison.
meta_desc: A-Level Religious Studies adventure on Bonhoeffer: Cost of Discipleship, Ethics, religionless Christianity, and resistance.
final_note: You have grasped Bonhoeffer's costly discipleship and its concrete shape in Nazi Germany.

walkthroughs.body_html: Published in 1937 as Nachfolge ('Following'), this book opens: 'Cheap grace is the deadly enemy of our Church. We are fighting today for costly grace.' Bonhoeffer reads the Sermon on the Mount as a literal call to obedience: 'when Christ calls a man, he bids him come and die'. The book was forged in the underground seminary at Finkenwalde, closed by the Gestapo in 1937.

Bonhoeffer's Ethics, unfinished at his death, rejects abstract principles in favour of concrete responsibility: 'who Christ really is, for us today'. He distinguishes the four mandates (work, marriage, government, church) and argues for the free responsible deed that may transgress conventional categories to serve the neighbour. He joined the Abwehr conspiracy against Hitler in 1940.

From Tegel prison, Bonhoeffer wrote to Eberhard Bethge that the world had 'come of age' and could no longer use God as a working hypothesis. Christianity must speak in a 'religionless' way - not abandoning the gospel, but ceasing to rely on metaphysical scaffolding. He was hanged at Flossenburg on 9 April 1945, days before liberation.

mcqs.q: What was the Augustine vs Pelagius dispute about original sin?
options: Original sin means Christians believe babies are evil.
Pelagius and Augustine agreed humans are born innocent.

Augustine argued humans inherit a corrupted nature from Adam (original sin) and cannot achieve salvation without grace; Pelagius argued humans retain free will to choose good without divine intervention and that sin is imitated, not inherited.
